cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. We're circling the station. I avoid my old office too. Why this route? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My former boss catches this train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I told mine I'd become a novelist. What did you tell yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That I had a better offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've carried the same blank notebook past mine for a year. Are you avoiding him because there wasn't a better offer?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 office avoidance, A3 novelist claim and A5 blank notebook are increasingly revealing bait, but the added authority line does not affect the route.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 former boss train and B4 better-offer claim fit avoidance; A5 blank notebook makes A own lie concrete without resolving B motive in advance.

relationship.evidence: B2 names the person avoided and B4 supplies the claim that makes the meeting uncomfortable.

heightening.evidence: B4 better offer prompts A5 the comparable sustained pretense and a motive question.

specificity.evidence: A1 station circling and B2 former boss establish the travel and social pressure.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 rank assertion add bulk without a travel concession.
